verdicts.reason: 6.1000 is a general intro-to-programming course (Python/OOP/complexity) that only demonstrates optimization/simulation at introductory breadth, whereas live OR-analyst intern postings expect substantive mathematical/optimization/simulation modeling as a core competency, so the incidental coverage is too thin to support the edge.

Live entry-level statistician postings explicitly require probability, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing (indeed.com/glassdoor), which are exactly the taught skills of 6.3700 Introduction to Probability (classical statistical inference, Bayesian estimation and hypothesis testing).

Business Intelligence analyst postings explicitly ask to 'identify trends and patterns from data' and build dashboards/visualizations from real datasets (indeed.com BI job description, ziprecruiter), matching 6.C35-J's taught skills of data visualization design and communicating insights from real-world big data.

OR-analyst intern postings require developing mathematical models, running simulations, and optimization projects (Lockheed Martin/ziprecruiter listings), and 6.100B is a computational-modeling course whose core topics are explicitly optimization problems and simulation models.

Data-engineer intern postings list Apache Spark, NoSQL/SQL databases, ETL pipelines, and scalable/big-data systems as must-have skills (indeed.com data-engineer job description, glassdoor), matching 6.1830's taught skills of scalable database systems (relational, NoSQL, Spark), data cleaning/integration, and production data-processing tools.

Live analytics-engineer postings (Mirakl, Crexi) center on dbt models, semantic-layer/data modeling, and advanced warehouse SQL, which 6.1830 does not teach; its systems focus (Spark, NoSQL, data cubes) does not correspond to the modeling-layer subject matter analytics-engineer roles actually require.

Statistician postings require hypothesis testing, regression, and validated statistical inference (indeed.com/glassdoor), directly matching 6.3720's taught hypothesis testing with multiple-comparison procedures, regression, and model validation/uncertainty quantification.

Data-scientist intern postings emphasize feature selection/engineering, regression/classification, and rigorous model validation/evaluation (enhancv/indeed data-science-intern listings), matching 6.3720's taught data exploration and feature selection, regression, classification, and model validation.

ML-engineer intern postings (Neuralink, Cloudflare, Lucid via the postings corpus) require designing/building ML models, deep-learning frameworks, and model evaluation, matching 6.C01's taught supervised/unsupervised and neural machine learning with emphasis on evaluating ML models.

Data-scientist intern postings require designing, training, and validating machine-learning models and selecting appropriate algorithms (indeed/enhancv), which is exactly 6.C01's subject matter of framing ML tasks and evaluating ML models.

ML-engineer postings prize an end-to-end ML project with model design, robustness, and evaluation (corpus web-ml-engineer postings; Gusto/Neuralink), matching 6.C011's project-oriented deep dives into ML method design, robustness, interpretability, and recommender systems.

Statistician postings require probability, statistical inference, hypothesis testing, and regression (indeed.com/glassdoor entry-level statistician listings), matching 18.05's taught probability/Bayesian inference, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, bootstrapping, and regression.
